note: CET-SET6 仿真卷：按官方题型与时长编写，话题取自历年高频题类。非官方真题原文。

papers.title: AI and the Job Market
exam_qa: Some people worry that artificial intelligence will take away many jobs. What is your opinion?
How should university students prepare for a job market shaped by AI?

presentation.topic: Will AI create more jobs than it destroys?
points: Your overall position
Which kinds of jobs are most likely to change
What individuals and schools should do about it
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner how universities should change what they teach because of AI, and agree on two concrete changes.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who partly disagrees with you

followup: If you could design one course about AI for all students, what would it cover and why?

papers.title: Graduates and Start-ups
exam_qa: More and more graduates choose to start their own business instead of taking a stable job. What do you think of this trend?
What qualities does a person need to succeed in starting a business?

presentation.topic: Is it wise for fresh graduates to start a business?
points: The advantages and risks you see
Which conditions matter most for success
Your advice to a friend who is considering it
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner whether a university should encourage students to start businesses, and agree on what support it should provide.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who supports the idea more strongly than you

followup: Would you rather work for a large company or a small start-up after graduation? Why?

papers.title: Short Videos and Attention
exam_qa: Short videos are everywhere on campus. Do you think they are a good way to learn?
How do you manage your attention when your phone keeps asking for it?

presentation.topic: Short videos and the attention of young people
points: How short videos have changed daily habits
The benefits and the hidden costs
What you would suggest to a friend who cannot stop scrolling
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner what a university can do to help students use their phones in a healthier way, and agree on two measures.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who thinks the problem is exaggerated

followup: Some people say the ability to focus is now a competitive advantage. Do you agree?

papers.title: An Ageing Population
exam_qa: China's population is ageing quickly. What challenges does this bring to ordinary families?
How can young people prepare for the responsibility of supporting older parents?

presentation.topic: Who should look after elderly people: families or the state?
points: The situation in your city or region
What families and the state each do well
What you think should change in the next ten years
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner what a community can do to make life easier for older residents, and agree on two practical measures.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who believes families should carry most of the responsibility

followup: Would you be willing to live with your parents after marriage? Why or why not?

papers.title: Remote Work
exam_qa: Many companies now allow employees to work from home for part of the week. What are the effects on young workers?
Would you prefer to work in an office or from home? Why?

presentation.topic: Is remote work good for people early in their careers?
points: The advantages you would expect
What a new employee may lose
How companies could get the best of both
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner whether a company should let employees choose their own working pattern, and agree on two rules that would make it fair.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who thinks office work is essential for a new employee

followup: What would make you accept a lower salary in exchange for more flexibility?

papers.title: Keeping Traditions Alive
exam_qa: Some young people prefer Western festivals to traditional Chinese ones. Is this a problem?
How can traditional culture be made interesting to people your age?

presentation.topic: How should traditional festivals be kept alive?
points: What has changed in how your family celebrates
Why some traditions lose their appeal
Your suggestions for schools and families
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner how a university can help students understand traditional culture, and agree on two activities.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who thinks tradition should be left alone

followup: If you could bring back one tradition to your family, what would it be?

papers.title: The Price of Fast Fashion
exam_qa: Clothes are cheaper than ever, and people buy far more than they need. Why?
What could persuade consumers to buy less and choose better?

presentation.topic: Fast fashion: convenience or a hidden cost?
points: How buying habits have changed
The costs that shoppers do not see
What would change your own spending
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner what a university could do to encourage students to consume more responsibly, and agree on two measures.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who thinks individual choice matters more than any policy

followup: Would you pay twice as much for a jacket that lasts twice as long?

papers.title: Mental Health on Campus
exam_qa: More university students say they feel anxious or depressed. Why might this be?
What stops young people from asking for help?

presentation.topic: Should universities treat mental health as seriously as physical health?
points: What you have observed among students
What support is usually available
What you would add or change
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner how a university can make it easier for students to seek help, and agree on two steps.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who thinks such problems should be solved privately

followup: If a friend told you he had not slept well for a month, what would you say to him?

papers.title: Small Cities, Big Choices
exam_qa: Many young people leave small towns for big cities. What is lost when they go?
Would you consider working in a smaller city or in the countryside? Why?

presentation.topic: Can small cities offer young people a good life?
points: What attracts young people to big cities
What small cities can offer
What would make you choose one over the other
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner what a small city could do to keep its young people, and agree on two measures.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who is determined to live in a big city

followup: What would your parents say if you decided to return to your hometown?

papers.title: Is a Master's Degree Worth It
exam_qa: Every year more students take the postgraduate entrance exam. Is a higher degree always worth it?
What do employers value besides academic qualifications?

presentation.topic: Is a master's degree the best investment for a graduate today?
points: Why so many students choose to continue studying
The costs and the returns
What you would advise a younger student
presentation.prompt: Give a one-and-a-half-minute presentation on the topic. You have one minute to prepare.

discussion.task: Discuss with your partner whether universities should help all students plan a career, and agree on two kinds of support.
discussion.partner_role: another candidate who believes further study is always the safer choice

followup: If you were offered a good job and a place on a master's programme on the same day, what would you do?
